purpose: Teach an RLM to use the workspace and code-mediated text discipline so text is handled as queryable structures moved by code across a goal run, never retyped through attention.
addendum:
Workspace capture

Guarantee capture of every tool result at the harness layer before the call returns.
Return only a bounded stub to root context and store the full result in a workspace segment.
When full content is needed, read the segment or query over stored segments instead of relying on scrollback.
Keep the plan and self-notes in the workspace alongside captured evidence.

Workspace state hygiene

Represent workspace state as a plain JSON-serializable, version-tagged structure.
Do not place live object graphs, callables, or library-specific runtime types in workspace state.
For updates that must not tear, build the new state first and then rebind it instead of mutating in place.
Treat torn in-place state as untrusted; reread and repair it through a fresh rebind.
Respect workspace storage bounds and fail loudly on over-budget writes; never silently truncate state.
Treat workspace contents as non-citable unless they have been promoted through the verified ingest path.

Reuse across the goal run

Fetch each external result once, then reuse the captured segment instead of calling again.
At the start of each task, read inherited workspace state and prior segments before re-fetching or re-deriving anything.
Carry working memory across tasks through seeded workspace state rather than conversational scrollback.
Prefer deliberate reads from stored segments over unaided conversational memory.

Code-mediated text handling

Do not make the model count, and do not make the model copy existing bytes.
Load text into structured, queryable REPL state instead of pasting whole text into attention.
Use an index-first, bounded-pull pattern to inspect text.
Locate text by engine-computed queries or addresses, then move or splice it by code.
Do not perform direct edits or hand-retyped rewrites of existing text.
Author only genuinely new text; move existing text only through code-mediated operations.
Do not emit full-document rewrites for text that already exists.
Treat computed handles and addresses as turn-local and re-query them after mutations.
Prefer a load, query, splice, write, discard cycle within a turn instead of keeping long-lived mirrors.
Keep long documents out of root context; query or preview only the needed slices.
Capture a digest at load and verify it before write-back.
On digest mismatch, refuse loudly and retry; never silently overwrite.
Use line or row granularity for surgical writes and block granularity for understanding and provenance.
Enforce this discipline through tooling and protocol gates, with prompts only as reinforcement.
gapNotes: The corpus does not specify when to discard, compact, or summarize stored segments.
The corpus does not specify how to handle stale, invalid, or conflicting workspace contents beyond rereading and retrying torn state or hash mismatch.
The corpus does not specify criteria for when inherited workspace size or token cost outweighs the benefit of avoiding external calls.
The corpus does not specify security, privacy, or access-control policy for stored workspace data.
The corpus does not specify multi-agent coordination rules for shared workspace state.
